notes.title: Day One: Feedback
notes.notes:
Hey, adventurers!

So, first off, thank you for playing [i]Absolute Tactics: Daughters of Mercy[/i]! It’s very exciting to see players enjoying our game! And I especially want to thank you all for taking the time to leave your feedback.

Let’s start talking about some of the feedback that I’ve been hearing and addressing them!

[b]Graphic Settings[/b] - This has been one of the most requested features from players. FPS limits, resolution options, Vsync, and other options. This has caused some issues for players and I’m bringing it up with the developers to see how we can implement changes to address these problems.
This is the number one priority on my mind for changes.

[b]Camera a Bit Too Close and Speed of Camera Causing Motion Sickness[/b] - While there is a setting in the options to bring the camera far away, I’m seeing players ask us to tweak this more. Also, the camera zipping across the map to view enemies plus the speed of the camera moving around with the mouse has been making some people nauseous. First off, we are sorry for any one that has gotten motion sickness. Secondly, know that fixing this is one of our top priorities.

[b]Extra Sound Settings[/b] - I’m hearing players ask for better control over the music, sound effects, and narrator’s voiceover in the game, with the ability to change levels on all three. We’ll look into this and see what kinds of changes can be made.

[b]Steam Cloud Support[/b] - I saw that some players wanted this option so they could play between laptops and PC or to have as a backup. I’ll ask if this option is possible!

[b]Hotkeys[/b] - Some players have asked us to add hotkeys for actions in battle to reduce the amount of clicking actions with the mouse. This makes sense to me, so I’m asking what it might take to implement hotkeys.

[b]Extra Data in Battles[/b] - This includes battle logs, enemy movement spaces, damage calculations before the attack, etc. This would help with strategizing and optimizing the best plan for attack. I definitely see why that’d be helpful and I am bringing it up!

Again, thank you all for your feedback! Hearing from you helps us improve the game and make it more enjoyable for more adventurers! I’m bringing everything in the above to the developers to see what we can do to support the changes requested.

Have a good weekend! 
-Riv Otter

notes.title: Slash through enemies in Absolute Tactics Today!
notes.notes:
Hey adventurers

[i]Absolute Tactics: Daughters of Mercy[/i] is out now!

[i]Absolute Tactics: Daughters of Mercy[/i] is a charming, turn-based RPG adventure that puts a modern spin on classic tactics-style games. Featuring a diverse cast of characters, enormous boss monsters, and a dark world embroiled in war, Absolute Tactics: Daughters of Mercy plunges players right into the action as our hero Huxley and his dog Max build their team of friends and allies to defend their home against a mysterious invading army.

Control your units and make use of their unique traits to dominate your enemies with masterful strategies which take advantage of unit placement, varied attack patterns, and skills that are as unique as each character. A vast array of deadly enemies, traps, puzzles and obstacles await to challenge you on your adventure.

https://youtu.be/ff6vioyuIHk

Features:
[b]Content Rich[/b] - Dozens of narrative story maps plus optional maps, including additional post-game content and horde mode!
[b]Challenge Yourself[/b] - Three levels of difficulty, plus an additional hardcore mode unlocked after completion - challenge yourself over and over again.
[b]Genre-Bending Gameplay[/b] - Shaking up the SRPG experience with diverse gameplay, including large-scale War levels (with dozens of units on the battlefield simultaneously), environmental verticality, puzzle elements and traps!
[b]Deeply Customizable [/b]- Accessible, class-based gameplay for the casual player combined with deep customization and mastery for serious tactics fans. 21 individual classes plus the ability to dual-class allows for almost endless combinations.
[b]Grow Your Character[/b] - Unlock upgrades, collect loot, complete quests, and meet a cast of colorful characters on your quest for glory.


You can also pet Max the dog! He’s a good dog.

-Riv Otter

notes.title: Strategy puzzler Absolute Tactics scratches my XCOM itch, until the characters start talking
notes.notes: Absolute Tactics: Daughters of Mercy doesn’t waste any time when you press start. Smash through a simple tutorial and within a few minutes you’re an amateur general, frantically issuing commands to your motley crew of D&D archetypes. Combat plays out as a dance, lunging forward to deliver crushing blows and recoiling back to pass out combat buffs to your squad. Unfortunately, that dance can lose a lot of its momentum when knock-off Edward Elric protagonist Huxley flips his shounen switch on and takes you back to 2005... Read more.

notes.title: The PC strategy RPG army swells: Absolute Tactics arrives September 15
notes.notes: Absolute Tactics, or as it would've been called in '90s California, Hella Tactics, is an indie project that longtime Gearbox Software developer Jason Shields has been working on for the last five years. It's finally almost finished, and landing on Steam and the Nintendo Switch on September 15—right in the middle of the biggest year for the strategy RPG genre in decades... Read more.

notes.title: Absolute Tactics Devlog: Story Missions and Bonus Missions
notes.notes:
Hey, adventurers!

It's me, Buddy, coming to hang out and show off some cool new [i]Absolute Tactics: Daughters of Mercy[/i] content as we get closer to release! This devlog actually comes from the Discord, (which you should [url=https://discord.gg/akuparagames]join[/url] if you haven't,) The question was: [b]How many levels are there in [i]Absolute Tactics[/i] and how do they work?[/b]

The quick and dirty answer? [b]25![/b] The longer, more complicated answer is down below!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40646320/5b9c294d4269282456cbfe1c79de9e82200d6f38.jpg[/img]

[h3]Story Missions[/h3]

[i]Absolute Tactics[/i] features a full narrative following the adventures of Huxley, Max, and their friends going up against the forces of Father Eldritch and his (eponymous) daughters of Mercy. That unfolds through twenty-five missions each in unique, hand-made maps. Some maps will have environmental hazards, some will split the party between two starting locations and some will feature massive, sprawling battles between the Forces of Father Eldritch and the Corliss Town Guard. 

But the core defining trait of Story Missions is twofold: 

1) You only play each Story Mission once!

2) Story Missions include the deepest mechanical progression with rewards like new Class Handbooks, capital, consumables and, most importantly, new team members added to your roster. 

Story Missions are going to be the backbone of any [i]Absolute Tactics[/i] playthrough. They're going to set the pace and give you the lion's share of the experience, items and power that you'll be using throughout the game. But they aren't the only missions in [i]Absolute Tactics.[/i] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40646320/f8e40ffbcff459fab473f8b7d5522316fdd2b0e2.png[/img]

[h3]Bonus Missions[/h3]

If you are looking for repeatable missions to round out experience, gold, or maybe even some consumables in a level, though, you will have access to that kind of repeatable content! Bonus missions in [i]Absolute Tactics[/i] get unlocked when you complete an associated Story Mission, which means from then on you'll be able to run the associated Bonus Mission as many times as you prefer! The good news is, that means you'll always have access to something to farm, especially if you find yourself falling behind in levels or power in the Story Missions. The bad news is, Bonus Missions tend to be less lucrative than a true blue Story Mission. 

Bonus Missions are set on some of the same maps as the Story Missions, but they're typically remixed compared to what players might expect when they're replaying maps they've beaten before. Maybe the player will start from the opposite side of the room. Maybe the configuration of enemies, traps or chests has changed significantly. Maybe a global mechanic present in the Story Mission doesn't show up in the corresponding Bonus Mission or vice versa. It's a good balance between what you might expect replaying a map and what you'll have to adapt to!

Bonus Missions also carry a single, enticing secret to be gained by investigative players! I won't spoil too much about secrets since part of the fun is letting players figure them out on their own, but I will say that the secrets are trackable in the UI so if you have successfully found the secret (or failed to find the secret) that will be readily apparent to you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40646320/65d5347cd5fd5a2ec7b65f7716774a2f4a46a2de.jpg[/img]

[h3]Hordes of Mercy[/h3]

Last but not least, there is one final game type that I'd like to give a little preview of! Hordes of Mercy is a post-game unlockable game mode that pits your wit and strategy against waves and waves of enemies. Like other horde modes in other titles, Hordes of Mercy will let you fight until you lose, granting you rewards for how long you and your team are able to hold out. 

How will you build the most effective squad? How will you prepare for the onslaught of enemies? How will you turn the tables when things get dire? You can find out more when we play Hordes of Mercy in a future livestream! 

That's everything that I wanted to show off today! Make sure you take a peek at the livestream on the [url=https://twitch.tv/akuparagames]Akupara Games Twitch[/url] channel this Friday at 10AM Pacific!

notes.title: Akupara Reveals Absolute Tactics: Daughters of Mercy
notes.notes:
Today, Akupara Games announces its partnership with Curious Fate to publish Absolute Tactics: Daughters of Mercy! 

Known for his work on the Borderlands series and as Creative Director of Curious Fate, Jason Shields has put together one of the coolest turn-based tactics games we’ve ever seen. With plenty to offer to both hardcore fans of the genre and newcomers alike, we cannot wait to show off more from Absolute Tactics! Expect a base difficulty that offers a respectable challenge for those new to the genre, but plenty for most diehard fans to sink their teeth into. 

[previewyoutube=DQT7KyVoyso;full][/previewyoutube]

Absolute Tactics: Daughters of Mercy puts a modern spin on classic tactics-style games. Featuring a diverse cast of characters, enormous boss monsters, and a dark world embroiled in war, Absolute Tactics plunges players right into action as our hero Huxley and his dog Max build their team of allies to defend their home against a mysterious invading army.

Control your units and make use of their unique traits to dominate your enemies with masterful strategies that take advantage of unit placement, varied attack patterns, and skills that are as unique as each character. Furthermore, players will be equipped with an extensive class customization system, including the option to dual-class - resulting in deeper synergies and nearly endless combinations to push back the opposition.

Features: 
[list]
[*] 25 narrative story maps plus 11 optional maps, including additional post-game content and horde mode!
[*] Three levels of difficulty, plus an additional hardcore mode unlocked after completion - challenge yourself over and over again.
[*] Shaking up the SRPG experience with diverse gameplay, including large-scale War levels (with dozens of units on the battlefield simultaneously), environmental verticality, puzzle elements and traps! 
[*] Accessible, class-based gameplay for the casual player combined with deep customization and mastery for serious tactics fans. 21 individual classes plus the ability to dual class allows for almost endless combinations.
[*] Unlock upgrades, collect loot, complete quests and meet a cast of colorful characters on your quest for glory.
[/list]

A vast array of deadly enemies, traps, puzzles, and horrors await you on your adventure - Will you rise to the challenge to defend your city from peril? Absolute Tactics: Daughters of Mercy is set to launch in 2022!
